name: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet chemist and professor who proposed the 'framework' hypothesis and co-founded the molecular layering method.

name: Stanislav Ivanovich Kol'tsov
summary: Soviet chemist and graduate student of Aleskovskii who experimentally substantiated the molecular layering method.

name: Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet
summary: Russian educational chemical engineering institute where Aleskovskii studied and worked for decades.

name: Naval Research Institute
summary: Research institute in Leningrad where Aleskovskii worked as a research fellow after graduation.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: Major Russian university where Aleskovskii served as rector and organized the Department of Solid State Chemistry.

name: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
summary: Soviet national academy of sciences of which Aleskovskii became a corresponding member.

name: Supreme Soviet of the Russian Federation
summary: Legislative body of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic where Aleskovskii was a member.

name: Mary
summary: City in Turkmenistan where Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii was born.

name: Leningrad
summary: City in Russia where Aleskovskii studied, worked, and lived for most of his life.

name: Framework hypothesis
summary: Theoretical concept proposed by Aleskovskii in 1952 regarding the chemical structure of solids.

name: Molecular Layering
summary: Gas-phase layer by layer deposition technology co-founded by Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov.

name: Chemistry of highly organized substances
summary: Scientific school founded and supervised by V. B. Aleskovskii.

name: Anatolii A. Malygin
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and co-author of the source essay.

name: Victor E. Drozd
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and co-author of the source essay.

name: N. A. Kosygin
summary: Prime Minister of the USSR who became interested in ML after a 1977 Pravda article.
